title: Swap a dust filter under a sprung cover: hold the cover open by its pedal while the other hand swaps the filter
instruction: Swap the dust filter: with one hand press the pedal on the cover's tail down and keep it down, so the cover stays open; with the other lift the grey dirty filter out of its slot by its tab and drop it in the bin, then take the new white filter from its holder and lower it into the slot. Let the pedal up so the cover shuts, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Routine maintenance of machines, robot controllers and servers includes changing air-intake filters behind sprung covers that snap shut when let go; a technician holds the cover open with one hand while swapping the filter with the other. Robots that service other machines need exactly this kind of two-handed hold-and-swap.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A machine's air intake, fixed: a light grey sheet-steel housing 24 cm deep (18 to 42 cm forward), 23.5 cm across (from 21 cm right to 2.5 cm left of the centre line) and 10 cm tall, with a grille on its front. In its top, an opening 20 x 12 cm over a slot in which the old filter stands upright, held at its ends by rails. (2) A grey sheet-steel cover over the top, hinged along the housing's left top edge and sprung shut; its tail sticks out 9 cm past the hinge to the left, rising 15 degrees, with a black rubber pedal (5 x 3.5 cm) on its end. Pressing the pedal down swings the cover up (about 70 degrees with the pedal near the table); let go, it shuts. (3) The old filter, grey with dust: a pleated panel in a frame, 11 cm long, 1.2 cm thick and 3.5 cm tall, with a black plastic tab 3 x 1.2 x 3.5 cm on top, standing along the forward line in the slot, 30 cm forward and 13 cm right of the centre line, its tab's top 1.5 cm below the housing's top. (4) A new filter, the same but white, standing in a grey holder with end rails 37 cm forward and 26 cm right of the centre line. (5) A blue plastic bin (13 x 10 cm inside, 7 cm tall) 20 cm forward and 27 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 1.0: the new filter seated in the slot (its underside within 1 cm of the slot's floor, upright within 12 degrees), the old one in the bin, the cover shut (within 5 degrees) and both hands let go (each gripper's fingertip centre, TCP, at least 4 cm from the pedal and from both filters' tabs) and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the new filter seated and the old one in the bin, otherwise; 0.25: the old filter in the bin; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the cover and both filters still.
reset_notes: Put the grey filter back in the slot and the white one back in its holder; the cover shuts by itself.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the cover is one rigid plate with its pedal tail on a hinge with a spring; the filters are rigid panels (no pleats to flex, no dust); the housing is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
